title: Castling, and when you cannot
outcomes: Knows the four conditions and which attacked squares matter
Spots when castling is not available

steps.text: **Castling** is the one move where two pieces move at once. The king goes two squares toward a rook, and that rook jumps over to the king's other side. It tucks the king away and brings a rook into the game. You can castle toward the h-file (kingside) or toward the a-file (queenside).

steps.caption: White castles kingside: the king goes to g1 and the rook to f1. Black castles queenside.

line.say: The king goes to g1 and the rook jumps to f1.
Black castles the other way: king to c8, rook to d8.

steps.text: You may castle only if: the king and that rook have never moved; every square between them is empty; the king is not in check; and the king does not pass over or land on an attacked square. The rook's own path does not have to be safe.

steps.title: Same castle, a rook arrives
steps.prompt: A black rook lands on f3. Predict first: can White still castle kingside?
Which castling condition would you check last in a real game: moved pieces, empty squares, check, or attacked squares?
